decisions.reason: Although it has not recently been highlighted online, it is tightly linked to our core airfield lighting control know-how and installed base, so our strong R&D and service capabilities favor improvement or integration into broader solutions rather than withdrawal.

Even with limited recent visibility, the display builds on our surveillance and operational-systems knowledge, and our absorptive capacity makes it more likely that we learn from deployments and refine it than abandon it.

This training program is very close to our existing systems business, uses knowledge we already possess, and supports customer retention and better use of our installed solutions, so it is unlikely to be dropped.

The course is a narrow service offer and could be folded into broader training, but because it directly leverages our airfield ground lighting expertise and aftermarket relationships, we would generally keep it.

The collaboration tool fits our strategic move toward integrated, real-time and collaborative airport operations, and our system-integration capabilities and own R&D give us a solid basis to keep developing it.

As a flagship surveillance product closely aligned with our technology base and future direction, it is exactly the kind of offering our R&D and learning capabilities are designed to strengthen rather than exit.
